name: DataGrid
intent: An editable table: people click a cell to add or change its content, like rule conditions, line items or mappings.
usage: Use DataGrid when people enter or change data in rows, not just read it. It is one component: pass columns and rows as data. Each column has a type: text and number cells edit in place with a kit Input, select cells are a kit Select, formula cells open a kit FormulaEditor in the cell, date cells are a kit DatePicker, and readOnly columns only show. Click a cell or press Enter to edit; Enter or leaving the cell saves, Escape cancels, Tab moves to the next cell. rowNumbers adds a # column. canAddRows adds an Add row button under the grid, canInsertRows a + at the start of each row that adds a row under it, and canRemoveRows a remove button on each row. Columns are at least 160 wide unless they hug. The first column (and #) stays pinned when the grid scrolls sideways. setForAll on a column adds a Set for all menu under its title. detail makes rows expandable, with settings or sub-rows under each row. For read-only lists use Table. See contracts/datagrid.json for the full contract.

columns.itemShape: { key: string; header: string; type?: "text" | "number" | "select" | "formula" | "date"; options?: SelectOption[]; searchable?: boolean; searchPlaceholder?: string; placeholder?: string; readOnly?: boolean; hug?: boolean; width?: string; fields?: FormulaField[]; onCalculate?: (formula: string) => string; setForAll?: boolean; opensDetail?: boolean }
columns.note: type defaults to text. options for select. date cells are always a kit DatePicker (size sm); their value is an ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD, shown formatted, and placeholder fills the empty field. fields and onCalculate for formula, passed to the FormulaEditor. hug makes the column only as wide as its content; otherwise it is at least 160 wide. width is a CSS width. searchable adds a search field at the top of a select column's list that filters options by label, for long lists like a product catalog; searchPlaceholder names it (default Search). setForAll adds a Set for all menu under the column title: Use row 1 value copies the first row's value to every row, Clear all rows empties the column. opensDetail (on a readOnly column, with detail and detailCount) puts a kit Button holding a Count of the other values after the cell's value that opens and closes the row's detail, and the grid drops its toggle column. The open detail lines up under that column (at least --data-grid-detail-min wide, 360px) and slides back toward the start when it would run past the grid's visible edge: use it when the cell shows the first of several values, like the first rate band.

rows.note: Controlled rows, one value per column key.

defaultRows.note: Starting rows when rows is not controlled.

onRowsChange.note: (rows: DataGridRow[]) => void. Runs when a cell is saved and when rows are added or removed.

size.note: Row height 38 / 40 (editable cells keep 8px padding; Table is 36 / 40), header 40. Without a size it is md. A surrounding Density changes these sizes through the density tokens (Default values shown). Formula cells grow while they are edited.

line.note: The line under the header row: medium is 2px, thin is 1px. Every header takes it, with or without Set for all.

rowNumbers.note: A # column with each row's number.

canAddRows.note: An Add row button under the grid. The new row starts empty and its first cell opens for editing.

canRemoveRows.note: A remove button at the end of each row, named by a kit Tooltip.

canInsertRows.note: A + button at the start of each row, as in the Figma data grid, that adds an empty row just under it. Named by a kit Tooltip, like Add row below row 2. Pinned with # and the first column. Use it with canRemoveRows, whose button sits at the end of the row.

emptyLabel.note: Shown across the columns when there are no rows.

label.note: Names the grid for screen readers, and each cell's field, like Value, row 2.

stickyFirstColumn.note: The # column and the first column stay in place while the grid scrolls sideways; their end border is the same thin line as every cell. Put the column that names each row first.

detail.note: (row: DataGridRow) => ReactNode. Makes rows expandable: a toggle column comes first, and an open row shows this under it in one cell across the grid, kept to the grid's visible width. Return null for a row with nothing to show: it gets no toggle and cannot open, so the toggle itself says the row has more, like rate tiers. Put kit pieces in it: a Form of settings, a nested DataGrid (size sm) for sub-rows people edit like rate bands, or a Table (size sm) for sub-rows they only read. The grid's own cell look stays on its own cells, so a Table inside keeps the Table look.

detailCount.note: (row: DataGridRow) => number | undefined. With an opensDetail column: how many more values the row's detail holds, shown as a Count in the cell's button. A row with no number (or a null detail) gets no button and cannot open.

expanded.note: Controlled: ids of the rows whose detail is open.

defaultExpanded.note: Starting open rows when expanded is not controlled.

onExpandedChange.note: (ids: string[]) => void. Runs when a row opens or closes.

useWhen: People build or change rows of data in place: rule conditions, price tiers, field mappings, line items.
Short editable lists where a form per row would be slow.
doNot: Do not use it to show data people only read. Use Table.
Do not invent an EditableCell, GridRow or a table of loose inputs. Pass columns with a type.
Do not build your own expand arrows or a second table under a row. Pass detail.
Do not put a Form around each row. Save the rows from onRowsChange.
a11y: A native table named by label, with kit HeaderCell headers.

Each editable cell is a button named by its column and row with its value, like Value, row 2: 100. Enter or click opens a kit Input, Select or FormulaEditor named the same way, and focus moves into it.
Enter saves and Escape cancels; focus goes back to the cell. Tab moves to the next cell.
Remove row buttons are named Remove row 2 and show that in a Tooltip.
Set for all is a kit Dropdown under the column title; the header is still the kit HeaderCell.

With detail, each row that has one starts with a kit Button named Show details, row 2 (Hide when open), with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the open detail, a group named Details, row 2. A row whose detail is null has no button.
A date cell is a kit DatePicker named by its column and row, like Start date, row 2.
With canInsertRows, each row's + is a kit Button named Add row below row N; the new row goes right under it.
With an opensDetail column, the Count button is named N more, row 2, with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the open detail.
snippet:
<DataGrid
  label="Conditions"
  columns={[
    { key: "field", header: "Field", type: "formula", fields: accountFields },
    { key: "condition", header: "Condition", type: "select", options: conditions, width: "200px" },
    { key: "value", header: "Value" },
  ]}
  rows={rules}
  onRowsChange={setRules}
  canAddRows
  canRemoveRows
/>

examples.title: Conditions
examples.usage: Field is a formula cell, Condition a Select and Value text. Click a cell to edit it; add and remove rows.

examples.title: Line items
examples.usage: number cells align to the end. A readOnly column shows values people cannot change. Small size for denser rows. Quantity has Set for all under its title.

examples.title: Dates and details
examples.usage: Start and End are date cells. API calls opens to its rate bands, a nested grid with a Currency select, and starts open. Seat license has one price, so its detail is null and it has no toggle.

examples.title: More values in a cell
examples.usage: Tiered rates. Rate is a readOnly opensDetail column: Sandbox Environment shows its first band, USD 0–10,000: 1,800.00, then a Count button with 2, the number of other bands. It opens the row to every band in a read-only Table size sm, line thin, captioned Sandbox Environment: 3 rates in USD. Seat license has one price, so its detail is null: no button, and no toggle column.

examples.title: Empty
examples.usage: No rows yet: headers stay, and Add row starts the first one.
